item.title: Synergistic Spatiotemporal Regulation of Li + ‐Flux During Formation Enables Stable Solid‐Electrolyte Interphase for Ah‐Level Si/C Anode‐Based Quasi‐Solid‐State Lithium Batteries
item.description:
تنظیم هم‌افزای فضایی-زمانی شار Li+ در مرحله formation با الکترولیت ژلی پیزوالکتریک BaTiO3 و پروتکل پالس دوقطبی، SEI پایدار و عملکرد چرخه‌ای باتری لیتیومی شبه‌جامد Si/C را بهبود می‌دهد.
Small | 🔬 Research Article
💡 This work uniquely combines a piezoelectric BaTiO₃/PVDF-b-PTFE gel electrolyte with bipolar pulse formation to spatiotemporally regulate Li⁺-flux during SEI growth. This synergy yields a dense, high-modulus SEI, enabling Ah-level NCM811||Si/C quasi-solid-state cells with enhanced interfacial stability and cycling. It establishes formation-process engineering as a practical route to high-performance batteries.
🏷 solid-electrolyte interphase · Li+ flux regulation · Si/C anode · quasi-solid-state battery · bipolar pulse formation

Small | 🔬 Research Article
💡 This work first introduces hydroxyectoine, an extremophile-derived solute, as a multifunctional additive for aqueous zinc batteries. It uniquely dual-regulates the water hydrogen-bonding network and zinc interface, suppressing hydrogen evolution and dendrites. The result is ultralong cycling (7300 h) and high efficiency, offering a bio-inspired route to durable, high-performance energy storage.
🏷 zinc battery · hydroxyectoine · electrolyte additive · zinc anode · hydrogen evolution

💡 This study pioneers the encapsulation of protic ionic liquid [Dema][TfO] into ZIF-8, revealing unique host-guest interactions: pore expansion, hydrogen bond disruption, and reduced thermal stability. The fully saturated composite achieves superior ionic conductivity (1.09 mS·cm⁻¹ at 160°C), outperforming other IL@MOF conductors. This demonstrates protic IL@MOF hybrids as promising solid electrolytes, advancing anhydrous proton-conducting materials design.

Small | 🔬 Research Article
💡 This work bridges molecular and device levels by designing a triazole-based cobalt catalyst (CoTzN) for bifunctional ORR/OER. Covalent anchoring on carbon nanotubes yields a stable, selective four-electron catalyst operating across pH 7–14. It enables cross-platform rechargeable metal–air batteries, powering quasi-solid-state Zn-air (>450 cycles) and non-aqueous Li-air (80 cycles) devices, demonstrating translation of coordination-level design into robust hybrid electrodes.

💡 This study provides the first 3D microstructure-resolved quantitative analysis of PTFE-based dry-processed electrodes for sulfide ASSBs. It reveals that 0.2 wt.% PTFE induces SE coating on cathode particles, raising surface coverage from 35% to 59% and improving component homogeneity and transport pathways, enabling high areal capacity (6.42 mAh cm⁻²) at high loading—advancing practical high-energy-density ASSB commercialization.

💡 This work first proposes a conduction-nucleation competition mechanism governing Li deposition, then designs a self-adaptive soft carbon/Mg₃N₂ gradient buffer that converts in situ into Li₃N and Li-C/Li-Mg alloys. item.title: Single-Atom Ce Enables Interfacial Pathway Regulation of Fe2 Atomic Pairs in Alkaline Oxygen Reduction

💡 Atomically dispersed Ce regulates the interfacial water/proton environment around Fe2 atomic pairs, suppressing the competing 2e– peroxide pathway and enabling the 4e– route. This decouples the activity–stability trade-off, yielding 0.92 V half-wave potential, 1.6% peroxide, 96% current retention over 50,000 s, and 1100 h Zn–air cycling—establishing interfacial pathway regulation as a design strategy for alkaline ORR catalysis.

💡 Nanorod high-nickel cathodes (including LiNiO₂) achieve stable cycling up to 4.95 V, unlike microcrystal counterparts. The novelty is that bulk structural reversibility, enabled by the nanorod morphology tolerating H2–H3 interphase lattice mismatch, allows full H3-to-H2 recovery on discharge. This enables high-voltage operation without sacrificing energy density, offering a design principle for durable high-energy lithium-ion batteries.

It matters because it guides predictive design, operando characterization, and practical deployment balancing performance against inactive mass, complexity, and cost.

تقویت مکانیکی در سطح ذره، کاتد غنی از نیکل را از ترد به مقاوم به آسیب تبدیل کرده و پایداری چرخه در ولتاژ بالا را به‌شدت بهبود می‌دهد.
Small | 🔬 Research Article
💡 This work pioneers particle-level mechanical reinforcement of Ni-rich cathodes, achieving a fivefold crushing-strength increase and reduced stress accumulation, which suppresses fracture during high-voltage cycling. The strategy enables 81% capacity retention over 400 cycles versus 36.5% undoped, establishing mechanics-informed design as a generalizable principle for damage-tolerant high-voltage cathodes.
🏷 Ni-rich cathode · particle fracture · mechanical reinforcement · high-voltage cycling · H2-H3 transition

item.title: Sulfonated‐ TiO 2 Nanorod–Reinforced PEO Composite Solid Electrolytes for High‐Voltage Solid‐State Lithium Metal Batteries
item.description:

ENERGY & ENVIRONMENTAL MATERIALS | 🔬 Research Article | 🔓 Open Access
💡 Sulfonated TiO₂ nanorods actively promote LiTFSI dissociation via Lewis base sites, unlike passive fillers. This raises free Li⁺ from 55.27% to 61.27%, enabling 1.5×10⁻⁴ S cm⁻¹ conductivity, >5 V stability, and 1000 h dendrite-free cycling. The work establishes coupled 1D morphology and surface chemistry as a viable strategy for high-voltage solid-state lithium batteries.
🏷 solid electrolyte · PEO · sulfonated TiO2 · lithium metal battery · high voltage

item.title: Chemical-Delithiation-Induced Surface Reconstruction in Layered Oxide Cathodes for High-Performance All-Solid-State Batteries
item.description:

Journal of the American Chemical Society | 🔬 Research Article
💡 Chemical delithiation with NO2BF4 reconstructs Li-rich layered oxide surfaces into a cation-disordered, fluorine-incorporating subsurface layer, passivating the oxidative interface and eliminating cathode–solid electrolyte degradation. This enables ~300.3 mAh g–1 capacity and 82.3% retention over 1500 cycles in all-solid-state batteries, and the strategy extends to Ni-rich oxides, offering a universal interfacial design route for high-energy ASSBs.
🏷 all-solid-state battery · Li-rich cathode · surface reconstruction · chemical delithiation · interfacial degradation

item.description:

Angewandte Chemie International Edition | 🔬 Research Article | 🔓 Open Access
💡 This work introduces the first sulfonimide-based polymer of intrinsic microporosity (FAS-PIM) and directly compares it with flexible, non-microporous polysulfonimide analogs. Adding succinonitrile drives both architectures toward similar conductivity, thermomechanical properties, and reprocessability, despite differing conduction mechanisms. This establishes convergence between permanently microporous and transiently porous single-ion conducting electrolytes, offering design guidance for next-generation materials.

💡 This work introduces a Hofmeister-regulated amide-protonated pPAM hydrogel electrolyte that suppresses polyiodide shuttling and I⁺ hydrolysis in organo-interhalogen-mediated four-electron Zn–iodine batteries. It enables practical iodine loadings (28.3 mg cm⁻², 9.95 mAh cm⁻²), over 2000 cycles, and Ah-level pouch cells (305 Wh kg⁻¹), establishing a design principle for high-loading quasi-solid-state 4eZIBs.

item.title: Facet‐Induced Electron‐Bridge Enables Enhanced LiO 2 ‐Mediated Reaction Kinetics for Stable Lithium‐Oxygen Batteries
item.description:

💡 This work introduces facet-induced electron-bridge engineering via a Mott–Schottky built-in electric field to enhance LiO₂-mediated kinetics in Li–O₂ batteries. By tailoring electron density and sorption microenvironments, it precisely controls Li₂O₂ nucleation, growth, and decomposition, enabling extended cycle life and reduced overpotential. The strategy offers a general principle for accelerating electron transfer and regulating intermediates through crystal-plane and interfacial engineering.

This design suppresses dendrites and volume swings, enabling 2000 h cycling and 82.66% capacity retention after 300 cycles, offering a mass-efficient platform for high-energy lithium metal batteries.

💡 This work introduces dual-functional CMC-Li supramolecular bridges linking PDA-modified LLZAO fillers in PVDF-HFP, simultaneously dispersing fillers and regulating ion solvation. This mitigates space-charge layers, enabling trans-phase Li⁺ conduction through ceramic bulk rather than sluggish interfaces. The result is dendrite suppression, 1400 h cycling stability, and high-capacity retention, offering a generalizable paradigm for advanced composite solid electrolytes.

item.title: Central‐Atom‐Differentiated Solvent Chemistry Enables Anion‐Reinforced Solvation for Ultra‐Long Cycling Ah‐Level Sodium‐Ion Pouch Cells
item.description:

Advanced Materials | 🔬 Research Article
💡 Introducing ethylene sulfite into carbonate electrolytes differentiates solvent central-atom chemistry (sulfur vs. carbon), rebalancing solvent-anion competition to reinforce PF₆⁻ in Na⁺ solvation. This lowers desolvation barriers and forms inorganic-rich interphases on both electrodes, enabling a 2.34 Ah pouch cell to retain 81.29% capacity after 3500 cycles and operate from −20°C to 50°C.

item.description:

💡 Particle size non-monotonically governs Li transport in Li₆PS₅Cl conversion cathodes: rate capability first drops, then recovers in the ultrafine regime, alongside cycling stability.
